---
title: "SimilaritySearchEngine.jl"
lang: en-US
---

`SimilaritySearchEngine.jl` is an embedded, no-HTTP-required Julia API for running
similarity search *projects*: named, persistent collections of dense vectors, sparse vectors or
text documents backed by [SimilaritySearch.jl](https://github.com/sadit/SimilaritySearch.jl),
[TextSearch.jl](https://github.com/sadit/TextSearch.jl), and
[RocksDB.jl](https://github.com/sadit/RocksDB.jl). A script does `using
SimilaritySearchEngine` and calls its functions directly — no running server, no CLI
subprocess, no job queue. The trust boundary is just OS file permissions on a working
directory, the same as any other embedded database.

## What it gives you

- **Project lifecycle**: `create_project`, `open_project`, `close_project!` manage a
  project's on-disk RocksDB directory and the live search engine backing it.
- **A project says what it holds, and separately what holds it**: `engine=` is `DenseEngine`,
  `SparseEngine` or `FullTextEngine` — dense vectors, sparse vectors, text — and `backend=` is
  the index underneath it, defaulting to that engine's own (`SearchGraph`, `InvertedFile`,
  `BM25InvertedFile`). `payload_kind(engine)` answers the first question for a project you
  opened; `BACKENDS` lists the legal pairings.
- **Dense vector search** over a `SearchGraph` (an approximate, self-tuning graph index),
  or an exact `ExhaustiveSearch`/`ParallelExhaustiveSearch`, all sharing the same
  `append_items!`/`search` surface — for a `SearchGraph`, `append_items!` only stages raw
  vectors, and the (expensive) graph-connection step happens in a separate, explicit
  `index!` call, so a caller controls when that cost is paid.
- **Sparse vector search** over an `InvertedFile`, for vectors *you* encoded — a learned sparse
  retriever, a feature table, a set of ids. It takes `SparseItem`s of a dimension fixed at
  creation, under any distance that reads a sparse vector (cosine over the weights, or one of
  `Dist.Sets.*` over the nonzero positions), and there is no vocabulary, no profile and no
  tokenizer anywhere in it. BM25 is deliberately not among its distances: it scores from corpus
  statistics rather than from a vector, so it belongs to a text project.
- **Full-text search**, where this package does the encoding, over a `BM25InvertedFile` or a
  weighted `TextInvertedFile`, sharing
  the same `append_items!`(stage)/`index!`(build)/`ftsearch` surface as the dense case — the
  first `index!` call on a text project also fits its `TextProfile` from whatever's been
  staged so far, so there's no separate training step to call first.
- **A text model stated explicitly**: creating a text project requires a `textmodel`, and
  there is no default. Prefer `DefaultProfile(:es)` — the published profile for a language,
  refitted to your own corpus at the first `index!` call, so your weights are calibrated over
  millions of paragraphs and the stopwords, lemmas and query-expansion network are inherited
  rather than derived (`refit=false` keeps the base's language-wide vocabulary instead).
  `BaseProfile(p)` uses a profile you already hold. `FitFromCorpus(TextConfig(language=:es))`
  is the explicit "no base profile" escape, delegated to `TextSearch.fit_profile` and capped at
  `max_documents` to bound its cost — which makes its vocabulary thin, and that is not a
  decision to arrive at by omission. Queries then travel with a
  `QueryPolicy`: whether to correct their spelling against the vocabulary (`ftexplain`
  reports what was corrected, `correction=:off` undoes it) and whether to widen them with
  the profile's expansion network.
- **Typed in, typed out**: items are `DenseItem`/`SparseItem`/`TextItem` values and results are
  `SearchResult`/`StoredItem`/`ExistsResult`. No JSON-shaped dictionary is taken apart by key
  name on the way in or assembled on the way out; `meta` stays a free-form `Dict{String,Any}`,
  and `get_raw_meta` is the one raw path, reserved for the HTTP server.
- **Soft deletes**: `delete_item!` marks a document as logically deleted without touching
  the underlying index; search reports a `deleted` marker per candidate instead of
  silently hiding or backfilling it.
- **Recall calibration**: `calibrate!` runs `SimilaritySearch.jl`'s real hyperparameter
  search so later queries can ask for `minrecall=0.95` (or any other target) and get back
  a `BeamSearch` tuned for it.
- **Whole-dataset operations**: `allknn`, `fft` (diverse sampling), `closestpairs`
  (near-duplicate detection), and `bichromatic_kclosestpairs` (closest pairs across two
  collections) all run synchronously, in-process, against a dense project's index.
- **Incremental, per-field persistence**: every mutation writes only the storage it
  actually touched — a `SearchGraph`'s raw vectors go straight into a memory-mapped file,
  a soft delete never rewrites the index, and routine inserts never rewrite the whole
  engine state. See [Architecture](architecture.qmd) for the on-disk layout.

## Where this fits

This package is deliberately scoped to project lifecycle, core CRUD, calibration, and the
whole-dataset operations (`allknn`, `fft`, `closestpairs`, `bichromatic_kclosestpairs`).

It has two kinds of user, and the embedded API is the surface for both. A **Julia program** does
`using SimilaritySearchEngine` and calls these functions directly — that is a first-class use,
not a testing convenience, which is why the API takes and returns typed Julia values rather than
JSON-shaped dictionaries. The sibling **`SimilaritySearchServer`** is the other: it wraps this
same engine in a CLI and an HTTP server, and it is a *consumer* of this package rather than the
reason it exists. Development happens here first, at the engine level, and is ported there
afterwards — so a capability can exist here before it has a server counterpart (sparse projects
do today), and a project touched through either stays readable by the other, same on-disk
layout and same insertion/search/persistence semantics.
